summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM deployments scale, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028 (up from 15% in early 2026), as teams increasingly need to trace prompts, track token costs, evaluate output quality, and connect AI issues to broader application performance. Choosing the right tool depends on whether your priority is cost tracking, evaluation depth, unified infrastructure monitoring, or vendor-neutral instrumentation.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt/response chains, agent steps, token usage, latency, and evaluation metrics; tightly integrated with the LangChain ecosystem.
features: Per-trace and per-span tracing with detailed execution timelines
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; Enterprise custom. (Approx. £80/month at modest volumes.)
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that need deep tracing, evaluation, and agent debugging in one integrated platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests, token usage, costs, latency, caching, and rate limits via a proxy/gateway that sits between your app and the LLM provider.
features: Cost visibility and per-request cost tracking
Response caching to cut repeat costs
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier (10K requests/month); Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (adds SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA); custom Enterprise (SAML SSO, on-prem). Noted as the cheapest managed option at ~£20 for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams whose top priority is cost visibility, caching, and the simplest possible setup for monitoring LLM spend.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, inputs/outputs, evaluations, experiment runs, model performance, and the broader ML experiment lifecycle.
features: Weave for LLM app tracing and evaluation
Strong ties to the ML/model-training ecosystem
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; team and enterprise plans are usage- and seat-based with custom enterprise pricing (contact sales for volume deployments).
tools.best_for: ML and research teams that want LLM observability integrated with full experiment tracking and the model development lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM and ML production telemetry, traces, embeddings, drift, data quality, RAG performance, and evaluation metrics at enterprise scale.
features: Arize Phoenix open-source (source-available) tracing and evaluation
Extends long-standing ML monitoring heritage to LLMs
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free and open source (self-hostable); Arize AX cloud has a free tier with paid Pro and custom Enterprise plans based on volume.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing robust production telemetry, drift detection, and both ML and LLM monitoring in one place.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt versions, token/cost metrics, user sessions, and evaluation scores; a popular open-source, framework-agnostic option.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests, then usage-based (around £20 for 500K); Self-hosted around £30/month infrastructure plus ~2 hours maintenance/month. Pro and Enterprise cloud tiers available.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a cost-effective, open-source, framework-agnostic tracing and prompt-management platform they can self-host.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, and metrics via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, exporting to any OTel-compatible backend (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, etc.).
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and vector DBs
Exports traces/metrics to existing observability backends
Integrates LLM telemetry into broader APM stacks
tools.pricing: Free and open source; costs are only those of your chosen OTel backend. Traceloop offers a managed cloud with free and paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation to feed LLM telemetry into an existing observability stack.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., with Helicone or a semantic cache) so identical prompts don't incur repeat token charges.
Route tasks to the cheapest model that meets quality needs — use smaller/distilled models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Trim prompt and context size: remove redundant instructions, compress retrieved context, and cap max output tokens to reduce per-call spend.
Instrument and alert on token usage and per-feature cost so you can catch runaway loops, prompt bloat, and expensive agents before they inflate the bill.
